ACCUSED : 1. Muralidhar A s/o late Abbayyappa  aged about 56 years  2. Rajani Muralidhar w/o Muralidhar  aged about 48 years  both are r/at No.92  Bilekahalli, Bannerughatta Road  Bengaluru  (Represented by Advocate Sri.Prasad G V)

5. The offence complained of U/sec.120B, 420, 504 and  or proved 506 r/w 34 of IPC

This is the case registered on the basis of the charge sheet submitted by PSI of Mico Layout police station against the accused No.1 and 2 alleging the offences punishable u/s. 120B, 420, 504 and 506 r/w 34 of IPC.
2. Case of the prosecution in brief is as fallows;

The accused No.1 and 2 have entered into joint development agreement with CW5 to construct apartment in the Site No.200/1, 2nd Main Road, 4th Cross Road, Bilekahalli, Sarvabhaumanagar,
Bannerughatta Road, belonging to accused No.1 and 2.
The CW5 has built an apartment named Neha Legenda in the said site.
In the said apartment Flat No.G-4 situated at Ground floor, came to the share of the builder CW5.
But, the accused No.1 and 2 criminally conspired with each other and represented to CW1 that said flat came to their share and made him to believe the same.

The accused No.1 and 2 obtained Rs.7,00,000/- from CW1 to the account of accused No.1 by agreeing to sell the said flat to CW1 and also executed a TRIPARTITE AGREEMENT & SALE CUM CONSTRUCTION AGREEMENT in the name of CW1 on 17-08-2015, and the accused No.2 signed the said agreement as a witness.

After knowing that the said G-4 plot does not belong to the accused No.1 and 2 and it has came to the builder's share, on 05-08- 2016 at 11.00 am when CW1 went to the above apartment and asked the accused No.1 to return the money, then the accused No.1 abused CW1 with filthy language and threatened to take away his life.

3. On the basis of the complaint lodged by the informant CW- 1, case was registered against the accused No.1 and 2 and after completion of investigation IO filed charge sheet against the accused No.1 and 2 for the above mentioned offences.
4. After perusal of the charge sheet since there are sufficient materials which constitute the offences alleged, cognizance of the above said offences taken by VI ACMM Court.
The accused No.1 and 2 appeared before the VI ACMM Court and released on bail.
5. As per Notification No.ADM-1-04-2024 Dated 07-03-2024 by Hon'ble CMM, Bengaluru this case is transferred to this Court, Bengaluru.
6. Copies of charge sheet supplied to accused No.1 and 2 u/S.207 of Cr.P.C. Heard, the counsel for the accused No.1 and 2 on framing of charge.

Since, on hearing the counsel for accused No.1 and 2 and on perusal of the materials on record there are sufficient grounds for presuming that the accused No.1 and 2 have committed the alleged offences, hence charge for the above offence framed and read over to accused No.1 and 2.
The accused No.1 and 2 pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

Thereafter, in order to prove the accusation leveled against the accused No.1 and 2, the prosecution has examined 5 witnesses as PW.1 to 5 and got marked 9 documents as Ex.P1 to 9.
8.
Even after issuance of summons, warrant and proclamation the prosecution has not secured CW1 to 5.

Hence, CW-1 to 5 were dropped by rejecting the prayer of learned Sr.APP.
9.
The statement of the accused No.1 and 2 recorded u/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
They denied the entire incriminating evidence available in the prosecution evidence.
They did not chose to adduce defence evidence.

10. Heard the arguments of Sr.APP and the counsel for accused and perused the records.
11.

The following points arise for determination:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that accused No.1 and 2 in furtherance of common intention have entered into joint development agreement with CW5 to construct apartment in the Site No.200/1, 2nd Main Road, 4th Cross Road, Bilekahalli, Sarvabhaumanagar, Bannerughatta Road, belonging to accused No.1 and 2 and CW5 has built an apartment named Neha Legenda in the said site and Flat No.G-4 situated at Ground floor, came to the share of the builder CW5, but, the accused No.1 and 2 criminally conspired with each other to sell the same to CW1 and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 120B r/w 34 of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond in furtherance of common intention accused No.1 and 2 criminally conspired with each other and represented to CW1 that said flat came to their share and made him to believe the same and obtained Rs.7,00,000/- from CW1 to the account of accused No.1 by agreeing to sell the said flat to CW1 and also executed a TRIPARTITE AGREEMENT & SALE CUM CONSTRUCTION AGREEMENT in the name of CW1 on 17-08-2015, and the accused No.2 signed the said agreement as a witness and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 420 r/w 34 of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that on 05-08-2016 at about 11.00 a.m. CW1 went near Neha Legenda Apartment and asked accused No.1 to return the advance amount for which the accused No.1 in furtherance of common intention abused CW1 with filthy language knowing that their insult may cause breach of public peace and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 504 r/w 34 of IPC?
4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that on the above said date, time and place in furtherance of common intention the accused No.1 gave life threat to CW1 by committing criminal intimidation and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 506 r/w 34 of IPC?

14. It is the case of the prosecution that the accused No.1 and 2 have entered into joint development agreement with CW5 to construct apartment in the Site No.200/1, 2 nd Main Road, 4th Cross Road,
Bilekahalli, Sarvabhaumanagar, Bannerughatta Road, belonging to accused No.1 and 2.
The CW5 has built an apartment named Neha Legenda in the said site.
In the said apartment Flat No.G-4 situated at Ground floor, came to the share of the builder CW5.
But, the accused No.1 and 2 criminally conspired with each other and represented to CW1 that said flat came to their share and made him to believe the same.

The accused No.1 and 2 obtained Rs.7,00,000/- from CW1 to the account of accused No.1 by agreeing to sell the said flat to CW1 and also executed a TRIPARTITE AGREEMENT & SALE CUM CONSTRUCTION AGREEMENT in the name of CW1 on 17-08-2015,
and the accused No.2 signed the said agreement as a witness.

After knowing that the said G-4 plot does not belong to the accused No.1 and 2 and it has came to the builder's share, on 05-08-2016 at 11.00 am when CW1 went to the above apartment and asked the accused No.1 to return the money

,
then the accused No.1 abused CW1 with filthy language and threatened to take away his life.
15. The prosecution has failed to secure the presence of CW1 to 5 even after issuance of proclamation against them.
Therefore, the CW1 to 5 are dropped.
The prosecution has examined CW6 - Mohammad Imran as PW3.
The PW3 is the witness to the agreement and also eye witness to the incident.

The PW3 has deposed in his chief examination that he has put a signature to the sale agreement which is with the CW1, he has not handed over any document to the police and he do not know anything about the case.

16. The CW8 is the PSI who deposed about receiving case records from CW7 and visiting the place of incident and drawing mahazar on the spot and after obtaining permission from the V ACMM Court,
transferred to the case to Mico Layout Police Station.
In the cross examination by learned counsel for the accused CW8/PW1 has denied all the suggestions put to him.
17. CW9 is the ASI who is examined as PW2 has deposed about receipt of the case records from DCP office and registration of FIR and handed over the case records to CW10 for investigation.
In the cross examination by the learned counsel for the accused CW9 has denied all the suggestions put to him.
18. CW7 is the ASI who is examined as PW4 has deposed in his chief examination about receipt of complaint from CW1, registration of FIR and handing over further investigation to CW8.

sentences.text: 19. CW10 is the PSI who is examined as PW5 has deposed in his chief examination that he taken over further investigation from CW9, recorded statement of CW1 and also received the documents furnished by CW1, he also wrote a letter to the Manager of the HDFC Bank seeking copies of the documents submitted by CW1 at the time of obtaining loan and the Manager of the HDFC Bank has furnished the documents and said documents are received by PW5.

PW5 further deposed that he recorded the statement of CW5 and also received the documents furnished by CW5, he wrote letter to Manager of Indian Overseas Bank asking for bank statement of accused No.1 and received the bank statement from the said Bank Manager.
He further deposed that after completion of the investigation filed charge sheet against the accused.
In the cross examination by the learned counsel of the accused all the suggestions put to PW5 are denied and nothing is elicited to discard his evidence.

20. On perusal of the above evidence on record, it could be noticed that the PW1, 2, 4 and 5 are the police officials who have deposed regarding registration of FIR and filing of the charge sheet, after completion of the investigation.

The PW3 who is said to be an eye witness to the incident has not deposed anything in support of the prosecution case to prove the offences alleged against the accused u/s 420, 504, 506 and 120B r/w 34 of IPC.
In this case the complainant CW1 and 2 complainant/victim and his father and CW5 the developer are the material witnesses to prove the accusation levelled against the accused.

But the prosecution has failed to secure the presence of the said witnesses even after issuance of proclamation, therefore, by rejecting the prayer of learned Sr.APP.
21.

Since the prosecution has failed to examine the material witnesses i.e., CW1, 2 and 5, hence only based on the evidence of police witnesses PW1, 2, 4 and 5 it cannot be held that the accused have committed the offence alleged.
The PW3 though said to be an eye witness but he has not deposed in support of the prosecution case.
22. Therefore, in the absence of evidence of CW1, 2 and 5, absolutely there is no evidence on record to prove the acquisition levelled against the accused No.1 and 2.
In view of the above evidence on record this court has come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove the accusations levelled against the accused No.1 and 2 beyond reasonable doubt.
Hence, Point No.1 to 4 is answered in the Negative.
19. Point No.5:

For the foregoing reasons and findings on point No.1 the following order is passed;
ORDER
Exercising the powers under Section 248 (1) of Cr.P.C. accused No.1 and 2 are hereby acquitted for the offence punishable u/Sec.120B, 420, 504 and 506 r/w 34 of IPC.
In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C, personal and surety shall stand cancelled after 6 (six) months.
